newsitem.title: UK: UK short stg discount rates at 6.75 pct by March.
newsitem.headline: UK short stg discount rates at 6.75 pct by March.

text.p: UK interest rate futures, known as short sterling, took another hit on Thursday and are now pricing in interest rates of 6.75 percent by the end of March next year.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke raised base rates by a quarter-point to six percent on October 30, catching UK markets unawares.
But after a spectacular drop in October unemployment and a jump in underlying inflation, further rate rises could now be on the cards, analysts said.
The March short sterling future was trading at 93.19 by 1135 GMT, down six basis points on the day.
At that level, it is discounting three-month money rates of 6.81 percent by the end of March next year.
The December contract, down five at 93.50, is basically positioned for a half-point rate rise by the year-end.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George meet for their last monetary meeting this year on December 11.

With underlying inflation jumping to 3.3 percent year-on-year in October and unemployment tumbling by more than 40,000, taking the overall rate to a five-and-a-half year low of 7.2 percent, many analysts think tighter policy is called for.

"The BoE will certainly claim this report to be consistent with their calls for higher borrowing costs now," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica. "Speculation will certainly be on a 6.25 percent base rate at the next monetary meeting in December."
In last week's quarterly inflation report, the Bank said the government's 2.5 percent inflation target was unlikely to be met and rates would probably have to rise again.
